0: Interest aggregation: replace the existing readout with 0.9*h_last + 0.1*sum(w_t*h_t), where w_t is normalized over valid recurrent states and proportional to 2^(-(L-1-t)/5). This inexpensive, parameter-free pooling may retain recent supporting interests without diluting the latest intent. Apply identically during training and prediction across all four datasets; preserve input histories, embeddings, GRU topology, scoring, loss and optimizer. Train and load one model per dataset.
1: Training strategy: change only the learning-rate schedule to linear warmup over the first five epochs, followed by cosine decay from the existing peak learning rate to 10% of that rate at epoch 200. Smoother initial updates and gradual decay may reduce the observed validation oscillation, especially in Electronics. Keep the existing optimizer, batch size, dropout, weight decay, early stopping, architecture and loss; retain seeds 0/42 and one model per dataset across all four datasets.
2: Learning objective: retain the existing loss and add 0.1*mean(softplus(s_negative-s_positive)), averaged over the same valid targets and already sampled negatives. This modest pairwise term directly encourages positive candidates to outrank negatives while retaining the original training signal, potentially improving HR@10. Change no sampling, scoring, readout, embeddings, GRU, optimizer or schedule. Apply across all four datasets with one independently trained model per dataset.
3: Feature construction: multiply each existing input embedding at valid position t by 0.9 + 0.1*t/max(L-1,1), with positions numbered from zero in the available causal prefix; use scale 1 for singleton prefixes and leave padding zero. This bounded recency feature may emphasize current intent without changing history selection or adding parameters. Compute identically during training and prediction. Preserve embedding design, GRU, readout, scoring, loss and optimizer across all four datasets, with one model per dataset.
